title: above

messages.description: when left inlet value rises above the threshold value
when left inlet falls back to or below the threshold

ELSE/above.body: [above] sends a bang to the left outlet when the left inlet is above the threshold value. Conversely, it sends a bang to the right outlet when the left inlet falls back to the threshold value or below it. The threshold value can be set via the argument or the 2nd inlet.

title: above~

messages.description: when left inlet value rises above the threshold
when left inlet falls back below the threshold

ELSE/above~.body: [above~] sends an impulse to the left outlet when the left inlet is above the threshold value. Conversely, it outputs an impulse to its right outlet when the left inlet falls back to the threshold value or below it. The threshold value can be set via the argument or the 2nd inlet.

title: abs.pd~

messages.description: the left input to pd~ subprocess
the right input to pd~ subprocess

methods.description: start a subprocess, no symbol restarts last one

ELSE/abs.pd~.body: [abs.pd~] loads a pd file into a subprocess via [pd~] and makes things more convenient like making the subprocess able to receive MIDI data from MIDI devices connected to the parent process (thanks to [sendmidi]). Also, you can open the subprocess patch by clicking on the object.

title: add
ELSE/add.body: [add] starts accumulating input values to a starting sum value (0 by default). The starting sum can be set as an argument or via the 'set' message. You can reset the sum to the starting sum value with a bang to the right inlet.

title: add~
ELSE/add~.body: [add~] starts accumulating input values to a starting sum value (0 by default). The starting sum can be set as an argument or via the 'set' message. You can reset the sum to the starting sum value with a bang or with an impulse signal to the right inlet.

title: adsr.m~

messages.description: release value (can set the release parameter of [voices~])

ELSE/adsr.m~.body: [adsr.m~] is a MERDA module of [adsr~]: a polyphonic ADSR envelope with multichannel gate and retrigger inputs (a bang also retriggers). The other inlets are CV inputs for attack, decay, sustain and release, which go through attenuverters and add to the knob values, and a time multiplier for all time parameters. The right outlet sends the release value, which can set the release of [voices~].

title: adsr~

messages.description: gate value in MIDI velocity range (0-127 is 0-1)
signal retrigger via impulses and gates

flags.name: -minsus <float>
flags.description: zero or above sets minimum sustain time (default -1)

flags.name: -maxsus <float>
flags.description: zero or above sets maximum sustain time (default -1)

methods.description: nonzero sets to immediate release mode
zero or above sets minimum sustain time
zero or above sets maximum sustain time

ELSE/adsr~.body: [adsr~] is an attack/decay/sustain/release gated envelope. At gate on (transition from 0 to any value), the attack ramp is generated, then a decay ramp goes to the sustain point (specified as a ratio of the gate value). At gate off (transition from any value to 0), [adsr~] goes to 0 at the specified release time in ms.

flags.name: -bw
flags.description: sets resonance parameter to bandwidth in octaves

methods.description: center frequency in Hz for each channel
clears filter's memory if you blow it up
sets resonance parameter to bandwidth in octaves

title: allpass.filt~

methods.description: sets order (needs to be multiple of 2)
center frequency in Hz for each channel
clears filter's memory if you blow it up

ELSE/allpass.filt~.body: [allpass.filt~] is an allpass filter whose order can be set via the first argument (must be a multiple of 2). This is an abstraction that stacks many [allpass.2nd~] objects in cascade.

title: allpass.rev~

arguments.description: maximum and initial delay time in ms

methods.description: changes the max delay size (in ms)

ELSE/allpass.rev~.body: [allpass.rev~] serves as a reverberator, allpass filter and delay. By default, you can set a delay time and a reverberation/decay time in ms ("t60"), which is the time the impulse takes to fall 60dB in energy (but you can change this parameter to a gain coefficient).

title: amean
ELSE/amean.body: [amean] creates a list of arithmetic means. It takes a start point, an end point and the number of steps from start to end. The number of steps is the output list length -1 and represents the number of values until reaching the end. The minimum number of steps is "1".

title: any2symbol

messages.description: any message to be converted to a symbol

ELSE/any2symbol.body: [any2symbol] converts any message to a symbol message.

title: args

messages.description: arguments given in the parent patch (bang is empty list)

ELSE/args.body: [args] loads arguments of an abstraction and can also change them. This is useful for the management of a variable number of arguments in abstractions, and can be used to change/set them up.

title: arpeggiator
arp

messages.description: nonzero turns arpeggiator on, zero turns off

methods.description: nonzero sets to external trigger mode

ELSE/arpeggiator.body: [arpeggiator] takes note messages and arpeggiates on the currently held notes according to a BPM and a relative note duration.

title: asr~

messages.description: gate values in MIDI velocity range (0-127 is 0-1)
trigger at control rate (like an impulse)

flags.name: -minsus <float>
flags.description: zero or above sets minimum sustain time (default -1)

flags.name: -maxsus <float>
flags.description: zero or above sets maximum sustain time (default -1)

methods.description: nonzero sets to immediate release mode
zero or above sets minimum sustain time
zero or above sets maximum sustain time

ELSE/asr~.body: [asr~] is an attack/sustain/release gated envelope. At gate on (transition from 0 to any value), [asr~] goes from 0 to the gate value at the specified attack time in ms. At gate off (transition from any value to 0) [asr~] goes to 0 at the specified release time in ms.

title: autofade.mc~

messages.description: input signals to be faded in/out

arguments.description: fade types <quartic, sin, sqrt, lin, hann, lin, hannsin, linsin>

ELSE/autofade.mc~.body: [autofade.mc~] is an automatic fade in/out for multichanne inputs. It responds to a gate control and uses internal lookup tables just like [fader~]. A gate on happens when the last input value was zero or less and the incoming value isn't. A gate off happens when the last value was greater than zero value and the incoming value isn't! The maximum gain depends on the gate on level.

title: autofade2.mc~
ELSE/autofade2.mc~.description: automatic fade with indepent in/out times

messages.description: input signals to be faded in/out

arguments.description: fade types <quartic, sin, sqrt, lin, hann, lin, hannsin, linsin>

ELSE/autofade2.mc~.body: [autofade2.mc~] is an automatic fade in/out for multichanne inputs. It responds to a gate control and uses internal lookup tables just like [fader~]. A gate on happens when the last input value was zero or less and the incoming value isn't. A gate off happens when the last value was greater than zero value and the incoming value isn't! The maximum gain depends on the gate on level.

title: autofade2~

messages.description: input signal to be faded in/out
fade types <quartic, sin, sqrt, hann, lin, hannsin, linsin>
input signal to be faded in/out
a 1 or 0 is sent when the fade in/out is finished

arguments.description: (optional) fade types <quartic, sin, sqrt, lin, hann, lin, hannsin, linsin>

ELSE/autofade2~.body: [autofade2~] is an automatic fade in/out (with separate time for fade in/out) for multichannel inputs. It responds to a gate control and uses internal lookup tables for 7 different fading curves. A gate-on happens when the last input value was zero and the incoming value isn't. A gate-off happens when the last value was a nonzero value and the incoming value is 0 The maximum gain depends on the gate on level.

title: autofade~

messages.description: input signal to be faded in/out
fade types <quartic, sin, sqrt, hann, lin, hannsin, linsin>
input signal to be faded in/out
a 1 or 0 is sent when the fade in/out is finished

arguments.description: (optional) fade types <quartic, sin, sqrt, lin, hann, lin, hannsin, linsin>

ELSE/autofade~.body: [autofade~] is an automatic fade in/out for multichannel inputs. It responds to a gate control and uses internal lookup tables for 7 different fading curves. A gate-on happens when the last input value was zero and the incoming value isn't. A gate-off happens when the last value was a nonzero value and the incoming value is 0! The maximum gain depends on the gate on level.

title: autotune
ELSE/autotune.description: retune to a close scale step
ELSE/autotune.body: [autotune] receives a scale as a list of steps in cents and a base MIDI pitch value (default 60). It then retunes incoming MIDI pitches to the closest step in the scale.

title: autotune2
ELSE/autotune2.description: retune to a close scale step

messages.description: pitch value in cents to be retuned

ELSE/autotune2.body: [autotune2] receives a scale as a list of steps in cents and then retunes incoming cents values to the closest step in the scale.

title: avg

messages.description: number to add to the moving average

ELSE/avg.body: [avg] calculates the mean average of all received numbers so far. A clear message resets the object.

title: balance~
ELSE/balance~.body: [balance~] performs an equal power (sin/cos) stereo balancing.

title: bandpass~

arguments.description: resonance, either in Q (default) or bandwidth

flags.name: -bw
flags.description: sets resonance parameter to bandwidth in octaves

methods.description: center frequency in Hz for each channel
clears filter's memory if you blow it up
sets resonance parameter to bandwidth in octaves

ELSE/bandpass~.body: [bandpass~] is a 2nd order bandpass resonant filter. Unlike [else/resonant~], it has a maximum and constant gain at 0dB.

title: bandstop~

flags.name: -bw
flags.description: sets resonance parameter to bandwidth in octaves

methods.description: clears filter's memory if you blow it up
sets resonance parameter to bandwidth in octaves

ELSE/bandstop~.body: [bandstop~] is a 2nd order bandstop filter, it can also be used as a 'notch' filter.

title: bangdiv

messages.description: subsequent bangs until divisor value is hit

methods.description: resets the counter to the start value

ELSE/bangdiv.body: [bangdiv] outputs bangs when receiving bangs by sorting them based on a corresponding divisor value. The first bang in the count is output to the left outlet, while subsequent bangs are sent to the right outlet until the divisor value is hit, starting the cycle again. A starting value lets you start in the middle of a count. If the start value is negative, it adds that many counts to the first time a bang is output.

title: bassdrum~
bd~

messages.description: pulse(s) that set the accent and trigger
sets pitch in MIDI, velocity (0-127) and triggers

flags.name: -mode <float>
flags.description: sets mode: 0 is TR-808 (default), 1 is TR-909-like

methods.description: bass drum resonant frequency in Hz
sets mode: 0 is TR-808, 1 is TR-909-like
attack sharpness and amount of overdrive

ELSE/bassdrum~.body:
[bassdrum~] provides a simulation of classic bass drums (TR-808 and TR-909 like). This is extracted from the Plaits module from Mutable Instruments.

The 'level' message only matters for control triggers: with a gate or impulse input signal, the level is taken from the signal's absolute value.

title: batch.rec~

messages.description: signal inputs to record for each channel
outputs a bang when the object is done recording

methods.description: starts recording for given amount of time in ms. If no float is given, the last set value is used
sets file name (no symbol opens dialog box)

ELSE/batch.rec~.body: [batch.rec~] is a convenient abstraction based on [writesf~] and the 'fast-forward' message to pd that batch records to a sound file that you can load with objects like [sample~], [play.file~], [player~] and others.

title: batch.write~

messages.description: signal inputs to record for each channel
signal inputs to record for each channel
outputs a bang when the object is done recording

ELSE/batch.write~.body: [batch.write~] is a convenient abstraction based on [tabwriter~] and the 'fast-forward' message to pd that batch records to arrays (from an object like [sample~]).

title: beat2ms
ELSE/beat2ms.description: convert beat length ratio to ms
ELSE/beat2ms.body: [beat2ms] converts from beat length to ms according to a BPM value given as an argument or a right inlet. It's nothing but [bpm] with inlets swapped.

title: beat~

methods.description: set analysis window size in samples

ELSE/beat~.body: [beat~] takes an input signal and outputs a detected bpm value.

title: bend.in

flags.name: -ext
flags.description: only listen to external input source (default no)

methods.description: nonzero sets to listen only to external input source

ELSE/bend.in.body: [bend.in] extracts MIDI Pitch Bend information from raw MIDI input (such as from [midiin]). By default, output values are normalized to floats from -1 to 1, but you can change it to "raw" mode (output integers from 0 to 16383).

title: bend.out

methods.description: nonzero sets to listen only to external mode

ELSE/bend.out.body: [bend.out] formats and sends raw MIDI pitch bend messages. By default, it takes normalized values (floats from -1 to 1). An argument sets channel number (the default is 1).

title: bicoeff

messages.description: filter type: allpass, lowpass, highpass, bandpass, resonant, bandstop, eq, lowshelf or highshelf

methods.description: nonzero saves the filter settings with the patch

ELSE/bicoeff.body: [bicoeff] is a GUI that generates coefficients for vanilla's [biquad~] according to different filter types ("eq" filter by default). Click on it and drag it around.

messages.description: frequency, Q/slope and gain, then outputs the coefficients

sets a lowpass filter, optionally with frequency, Q/slope and gain
sets a highpass filter, optionally with frequency, Q/slope and gain
sets a bandpass filter, optionally with frequency, Q/slope and gain
sets a resonant filter, optionally with frequency, Q/slope and gain
sets a bandstop filter, optionally with frequency, Q/slope and gain
sets an eq filter, optionally with frequency, Q/slope and gain
sets a lowshelf filter, optionally with frequency, Q/slope and gain
sets a highshelf filter, optionally with frequency, Q/slope and gain
sets gain in dB and outputs coefficients

ELSE/bicoeff2.body: [bicoeff2] generates coefficients for vanilla's [biquad~] according to different filter types. All inlets are hot!

title: bin.shift~

messages.description: sets number of bins to shift

ELSE/bin.shift~.body: [bin.shift~] is meant to be used for spectral processing, where you can shift samples (or frequency bins). It is similar to Pd Vanilla's [lrshift~] object, which acts in any block size and shifts samples to the left or right.

title: biplot

messages.description: list of coefficients as taken by [biquad~]
list of coefficients is passed through

ELSE/biplot.body: [biplot] plots the filter response from biquad coefficients, the ones you send to [biquad~] or [biquads~].

title: biquads~

methods.description: <1> bypasses the input, <0> turns the filter on

ELSE/biquads~.body: [biquads~] is a series of biquad filters in cascade. Each biquad section is defined as a list of 5 coefficients (in the same way as Pd Vanilla's [biquad~]). The maximum number of filter stages is 50, which provides up to 100th order filters.

title: bitnormal~
ELSE/bitnormal~.description: replace NaN/Inf and denormal signals with 0

messages.description: input whose NaN/Inf/denormal values are replaced with 0

ELSE/bitnormal~.body: [bitnormal~] replaces NaN (not a number), +/- infinity values and denormals of an incoming signal with zero (hence, it only lets 'normal' floats through. This is useful in conjunction with the bitwise operators in [op~], [expr~] or any other situation where these values are possible.

title: bl.imp2~

flags.name: -midi
flags.description: sets frequency input in MIDI pitch (default Hz)

flags.name: -mc <list>
flags.description: sets multichannel output with a list of frequencies

methods.description: nonzero sets to frequency input in MIDI pitch
<channel, freq> sets a single frequency channel

ELSE/bl.imp2~.body: [bl.imp2~] is a two sided impulse oscillator like [else/imp2~], but it is bandlimited with the upsampling/filtering technique. This makes the object quite inefficient CPU wise, but is an easy way to implement a bandlimited oscillator.

title: bl.imp~

flags.name: -midi
flags.description: sets frequency input in MIDI pitch (default Hz)

flags.name: -mc <list>
flags.description: sets multichannel output with a list of frequencies

methods.description: nonzero sets to frequency input in MIDI pitch
<channel, freq> sets a single frequency channel

ELSE/bl.imp~.body: [bl.imp~] is an impulse oscillator like [else/imp~], but it is bandlimited.

nonzero sets to soft sync mode

ELSE/bl.osc~.body: [bl.osc~] is a bandlimited oscillator based on [wavetable~]. It has wavetables built with a variable number of partials for different waveforms: 'saw', 'saw2', 'tri', 'square' and 'imp'.

flags.name: -soft

<channel, freq> sets a single frequency channel

ELSE/bl.tri~.body: [bl.tri~] is a triangular oscillator like [else/tri~], but it is bandlimited.

flags.description: sets frequency input in MIDI pitch (default Hz)

flags.name: -soft
flags.description: sets to soft sync mode (default hard)

flags.name: -mc <list>
flags.description: sets multichannel output with a list of frequencies

methods.description: nonzero sets to frequency input in MIDI pitch
nonzero sets to soft sync mode
<channel, freq> sets a single frequency channel

ELSE/bl.vsaw~.body: [bl.vsaw~] is a variable sawtooth waveform oscillator that also becomes a triangular osccilator just like [else/vsaw~], but it is bandlimited.

title: bl.wavetable~

flags.name: -midi
flags.description: sets frequency input in MIDI pitch (default Hz)

flags.name: -soft
flags.description: sets to soft sync mode (default hard)

methods.description: sets an entire array to be used as a waveform
sets size in number of points

nonzero sets to soft sync mode

ELSE/bl.wavetable~.body: [bl.wavetable~] is a wavetable oscillator like [else/wavetable~], but it is bandlimited with the upsampling/filtering technique. This makes the object quite inefficient CPU wise, but is an easy way to implement a bandlimited oscillator. This object also minimizes aliasing caused by hard sync and phase modulation.

title: blip~

flags.name: -midi
flags.description: sets frequency input in MIDI pitch (default Hz)

flags.name: -soft
flags.description: sets to soft sync mode (default hard)

methods.description: nonzero sets to frequency input in MIDI pitch
nonzero sets to soft sync mode

ELSE/blip~.body: [blip~] uses DSF (Discrete-Summation Formulae) to generate waveforms as a sum of cosines. It takes a frequency in Hz for the fundamental, a number of harmonics, a multiplier for the partials after the first one and the lowest harmonic number (by default it generates an impulse waveform). This object is based on Csound's 'gbuzz' opcode.

title: blocksize~

messages.description: get block size period or frequency

methods.description: set and get the block size period in samples
set and get the sample rate period in ms
set and get the block size frequency in Hz

ELSE/blocksize~.body: [blocksize~] reports the block size when the audio is turned on, when it changes or via a bang. The period is reported in samples or ms, but you can also query the corresponding frequency in Hz. The default output is the block size in samples. The DSP needs to be turned on so a block size is detected!

title: bpbank~

messages.description: signal to be filtered via a bank of bandpass filters
the signal filtered by the bank of filters

flags.name: -freq <list>
flags.description: sets list of frequencies for all filters

flags.name: -amp <list>
flags.description: sets list of amplitudes for all filters

flags.name: -q <list>
flags.description: sets list of resonance (Q) for all filters

flags.name: -ramp <list>
flags.description: sets list of ramp time for all filters

flags.name: -rampall <float>
flags.description: sets ramp time for all filters

list of resonance (Q) for all filters in the bank
list of amplitudes for all filters in the bank
list of ramp time for all filters in the bank
ramp time for all filters in the bank

ELSE/bpbank~.body: [bpbank~] is a bank made of [bandpass~] objects. You can set any number of filters with the first argument and control the parameters for each filter. If you use flags, the number of elements in the list (such as the frequency list) sets the number of filters in the bank (you shouldn't use arguments if you use flags).

title: bpm
ELSE/bpm.body: [bpm] calculates a conversion to and from bpm (beats per minute). By default it converts to and from ms, but you can also set it to convert to and from samples.

title: bpm2hz
ELSE/bpm2hz.body: [bpm2hz] converts from BPM to Hz according to a beat length (default 1/4). You can change the beat length via the argument or right inlet.

title: brane.m~
ELSE/brane.m~.body: [brane.m~] is a MERDA module with a granular sampler that can stretch and compress time, and a harmonizer pitch shifter. The sampler records or plays mono files and runs two pitch shifters, for a root and a harmony voice. Unlike the other modules, it has its own preset system and doesn't save its state with the patch. The argument sets the recording time in minutes, or a file to load.

title: break
ELSE/break.body: [break] can break a list with a given symbol separator set via the argument.

title: brickwall~
ELSE/brickwall~.body: [brickwall~] a 10th order butterworth lowpass filter, which is filter with a steep cutoff slope (60 dB by octave). By default, its cutoff frequency is 0.75 * Nyquist, but you can change it with the 1st argument or the second inlet.

title: brown

messages.description: random value based on brownian motion

methods.description: a float sets seed, no float sets a unique internal

ELSE/brown.body: [brown] is a control brownian motion generator. It is a bounded random walk (based on a pseudo random number generator algorithm). By default, the maximum step is "0.125", which is a ratio of the whole range (and the output range is from 0 to 127). If it tries to step outside the bounds, it just gets folded back.

title: brown~

messages.description: impulses get a new random step

methods.description: a float sets seed, no float sets a unique internal

ELSE/brown~.body: [brown~] is a brown noise generator (aka brownian noise or red noise), whose spectral energy drops 6dB per octave (sounding less hissy than white noise). It is implemented as a bounded random walk (based on a pseudo random number generator algorithm). By default, the maximum step is 0.125, but you can set that. If a signal is connected, nonzero values generate new random steps.

title: buffer

messages.description: resize, set array and output list

methods.description: 1st item is index, the next are values from that index

ELSE/buffer.body: [buffer] does not much and nothing that [array] can't, but it's a convenient object for getting and setting array values, kinda like a storage object such as [message]. You can get/set arrays from actual arrays, [table] or [array] objects.

title: button

messages.description: when in bang mode, activates bang, change state otherwise
when not in bang mode, set state

flags.name: -size <float>
flags.description: sets both horizontal and vertical size in pixels

methods.description: flips the state and outputs it (toggle mode only)
sets the state without output (not in bang mode)
sets horizontal and vertical size in pixels
nonzero sets to oval style, 0 hides it
sets both horizontal and vertical size in pixels

ELSE/button.body: [button] is a GUI button that responds to mouse clicks. When clicked on, it sends a "1" value, and outputs "0" when releasing the mouse button.

title: canvas.active
ELSE/canvas.active.body: The [canvas.active] object outputs activity status. It sends 1 if the window is active (when it's the front-most window) and 0 when inactive. It can also query the parent status with the depth argument (1 goes up to the parent patch, 2 queries the parent's parent and so on).

title: canvas.bounds
ELSE/canvas.bounds.body: The [canvas.bounds] object outputs bounds coordinates in pixels, top left coordinate (horizontal, vertical) and bottom right (horizontal, vertical). Try moving the patch window or change window size to see changes.

title: canvas.edit
ELSE/canvas.edit.body: The [canvas.edit] object outputs edit status - 1 when the window is in edit mode and 0 when it is in run mode.

title: canvas.gop

messages.description: GOP info <gop status, x size, y size, coords (x1, y1, x2, y1)>

ELSE/canvas.gop.body: The [canvas.gop] object outputs the information of a "graph on parent" (aka 'GOP'), which is a subpatch with a visible graph in the parent. It can also query the GOP info with the depth argument (1 goes up to the parent patch, 2 queries the parent's parent and so on).

title: canvas.mouse

arguments.description: nonzero allows output in edit mode

ELSE/canvas.mouse.body: [canvas.mouse] gets mouse click and mouse coordinates when your mouse is interacting with the canvas window. An optional argument sets the depth level. This object doesn't output anything if in edit mode.

title: canvas.name
ELSE/canvas.name.body: [canvas.name] gives you the canvas/window name symbol.

title: canvas.pos
ELSE/canvas.pos.body: The [canvas.pos] object outputs the position of a subwindow canvas in the parent canvas. The output is the x/y coordinates. It can also query the parent status with the depth argument (1 goes up to the parent patch, 2 queries the parent's parent and so on).

title: canvas.setname
ELSE/canvas.setname.body: [canvas.setname] sets a symbol name to a canvas so you can send it messages. It's similar to [namecanvas] but it also allows you to set the name of a parent patch with the second optional depth argument - (1) is parent patch (2) is parent's parent patch and so on...

title: canvas.vis
ELSE/canvas.vis.body: The [canvas.vis] object outputs visibility status. It sends 1 if the window is visible and 0 when it's not. It can also query the parent status with the depth argument (1 goes up to the parent patch, 2 queries the parent's parent and so on). The object can react to most visibility changes and you can also query for it with a bang.

title: canvas.zoom
ELSE/canvas.zoom.body: The [canvas.zoom] object outputs zoom status at load time and when it changes - it outputs 1 when the window is in zoom mode and 0 when it is not. You can also query with a bang.

title: car2pol

messages.description: converts the last received coordinates pair
real part from the Cartesian coordinates

[dict.define] defines a container for dictionaries in JSON syntax. With a given name, the data is shared and can be accessed and changed by the other dict objects, such as [dict.get], [dict.set] and [dict.add]. Unlike [messcoll], [dict.define] objects must not share the same name.

Keys are symbols inside quotes followed by a colon, and values can be an atom, a list, a nested list or another dictionary. Nested keys are addressed by the other dict objects as a path separated by slashes, as in "key/subkey".

By default, the contents are not saved with the patch, but you can change that with the -k flag or the 'keep' message, which remains valid when reopening and resaving the patch. If a file argument is given, the keep flag and message are ignored, since the data is stored in the file.

Clicking on the object opens an editor window. Shift+click opens a dialog window to read a file, and alt+click one to save a file.

title: echo.rev~

By default, the first bang into the left input resets and arms the timer, and later bangs output the time since then without restarting it. If you give it a nonzero argument, the object is reset and armed at creation. The right inlet takes a bang that resets the timer. It is similar to Vanilla's [timer], but with a hot left inlet.

It accepts the "about" message that prints this basic information (version, release date, etc) on the terminal on demand and also accepts the "version" message that outputs the version information as a list.

title: expand~
ELSE/expand~.body: [expand~] is an abstraction that performs expanding. It attenuates an input signal below a given threshold.

title: factor
ELSE/factor.body: [factor] is a factorization function. It receives a float and spits a list of its factors.

title: filter
ELSE/filter.description: filter a float or symbol from a data stream
ELSE/filter.body: [filter] outputs an element to be filtered on the left outlet and the unfiltered ones on the right outlet. This is very similar to [select] but outputs the filtered element instead.

title: filterdelay~

methods.description: resonant filter cutoff in Hz (default 20 kHz)

ELSE/filterdelay~.body: [filterdelay~] is a high level delay unit that goes thgouh a resonant lowpass filter, a soft clipper and a DC filter. The processed delay output is also fed back into the delay line.

title: flanger.m~
ELSE/flanger.m~.body: [flanger.m~] is a MERDA module wrapper around [flanger~], a flanger effect. It has no CV inputs yet, so it works like an effect pedal.

title: flanger~
ELSE/flanger~.body: [flanger~] is a simple flanger FX object.

list of bits, or sign, exponent and mantissa after a 'split' message

ELSE/float2bits.body: [float2bits] converts decimal float (IEEE754 Single precision 32-bit) values to binary form (a list of 32 bits). By the way, this is the type of float used in Pure Data.

title: float2imp~

messages.description: set impulse value and generate impulse

ELSE/float2imp~.body: [float2imp~] converts floats to impulses with sample accuracy. It is an abstraction based on [vline~], so it can convert to an impulse within an audio block. A bang can be used to output the impulse with the stored value. The default value is '1' and can be set via the argument. The right inlet also sets the impulse value. A float input sets the value and gets converted to an impulse.

title: float2sig~
f2s~
ELSE/float2sig~.body: [float2sig~] (or [f2s~] for short) converts floats to signals. The conversion is smoothened by a ramp time in ms.

title: floor~
ELSE/floor~.body: [floor~] is a floor math function for signals.

title: fm~

messages.description: modulation frequency as ratio of carrier

arguments.description: modulation frequency as ratio of carrier

ELSE/fm~.body: [fm~] is a simple frequency modulation unit consisting of a pair of sinusoidal oscillators, where one modulates the frequency input of another. The modulation frequency is set as a ratio of the carrier and the modulation index is multiplied by this resulting frequency. The object has support for multichannels.

title: fold

messages.description: fold or output the last folded value (only float)

arguments.description: 2 floats set min and max, 1 float sets max value (min to 0)

methods.description: sets next value to be folded via bang (only float)

ELSE/fold.body: [fold] folds between a low and high value. This is like a mirroring function, where an out of bounds value folds back until it is in the given range.

title: fold~

arguments.description: 2 floats set min and max, 1 float sets max value (min to 0)

ELSE/fold~.body: [fold~] folds between a low and high value. This is like a mirroring function, where an out of bounds value folds back until it is in the given range.

title: follow~
ELSE/follow~.body: [follow~] is like [lag2~] being fed a signal passing through [abs~]. But secondary inlets are float only and it can output floats instead. Instead of up/down lag times we now have attack and release times. By default, the object outputs audio signals, but you can set a float output with the '-f' flag.

title: fonts

messages.description: available fonts or pd's font info list

methods.description: report Pd's font information (font name and style)

ELSE/fonts.body: The [fonts] object outputs all of your available fonts in your system. A 'pdfont' message outputs a list with Pd's font information (font name and style).

title: fontsize
ELSE/fontsize.body: The [fontsize] object outputs the patch's font size when the object is loaded and when it changes via the font menu. You can also query with a bang message.

title: formant~
ELSE/formant~.body: [formant~] is a formant oscillator based on SuperCollider's Formant UGen. You specify the fundamental (f0) frequency, the center (or formant) frequency and the bandwidth (around the center frequency). All these parameters are in Hz. This technique is used to synthesize vocal sounds. The object has support for multichannels.

title: format

messages.description: atoms for the format variables, extra items go to the next inlets

ELSE/format.body: [format] formats messages similarly to [makefilename], but it accepts more than one variable where each corresponds to an inlet. It also allows you to generate messages with more than on element.

title: formfm~
ELSE/formfm~.body: [formfm~] is a FM formant oscillator (actually phase modulation) where you specify the fundamental (f0) frequency, the center (or formant) frequency as a ratio and the bandwidth (as the modulation index). The object has support for multichannels.

title: formlet~

methods.description: clears filter's memory if you blow it up
resonant frequency in Hz for each channel
attack time in ms for each channel
decay time in ms for each channel

ELSE/formlet~.body: Based on SuperCollider's Formlet UGen, [formlet~] is a resonant filter similar to [resonator~] in bandpass mode (and [resonant~] by extension). The difference is that you can also specify an attack time besides the decay time. An advantage to this filter over FOF is that there is no limit to the number of overlapping grains.

title: frac.add

fractional value to add to left input

ELSE/frac.add.body: Use [frac.add] to add two fractions. The output is also a fraction.

title: frac.mul

fractional value to multiply to left input

ELSE/frac.mul.body: Use [frac.mul] to multiply two fractions. The output is also a fraction.

title: frac2cents
ELSE/frac2cents.body: Use [frac2cents] to convert a list of intervals defined as fraction symbols to cents.

title: frac2dec
ELSE/frac2dec.body: Use [frac2dec] to convert a single element or list of intervals defined as fraction symbols to decimal floating point numbers. Numbers don't need to be integers and you can also have a second fraction between parenthesis as the denominator or numerator.

title: free.rev~
ELSE/free.rev~.body: [free.rev~] is a stereo reverb abstraction based on the widely known 'freeverb' algorithm.

title: freeze~
ELSE/freeze~.body: [freeze~] is an abstraction based on [sigmund~] (analysis & resynthesis). It contains a bank with oscillators.

title: freq.shift~

signal shifted in the opposite direction

ELSE/freq.shift~.body: [freq.shift~] has two outputs, the left outlet is the frequency shifted signal and the right outlet is the signal shifted in the opposite direction.

title: freq2midi

messages.description: set a new value for A4

ELSE/freq2midi.body: [freq2midi] converts frequency to MIDI like [ftom], but it also converts lists and allows you so set a different frequency reference value for A4 so you can explore different tunings.

title: function

ELSE/function.body: [function] is a breakpoints function GUI, mainly used with [function~] or [envgen~]. You can click and drag on it or send it lists.

ELSE/function~.body: [function~] generates functions from arguments/list input. Input values from 0 to 1 reads the function. It needs an odd number of elements in a list, staring with 3 values, the syntax is (point1, period, point2, period, point3, etc...). The overall sum of periods is normalized to 1!

title: gate2imp~
ELSE/gate2imp~.body: [gate2imp~] converts gates to impulses. It sends an impulse when receiving a gate (0 to nonzero transitions) where the impulse value is the same as the gate.

title: gatedelay
ELSE/gatedelay.body: [gatedelay] delays a control gate on value, but the gate off is immediately output.

title: gatedelay~
ELSE/gatedelay~.body: [gatedelay~] delays a gate on value, but the gate off is immediately output. The object has support for multichannels

title: gatehold
ELSE/gatehold.body: [gatehold] holds a gate value for a certain amount of time (specified in ms) after the gate has closed. If a new gate starts before the hold time is finished, the object is retriggered.

title: gatehold~
ELSE/gatehold~.body: [gatehold~] holds a gate value for a certain amount of time (specified in ms) after the gate has closed. If a new gate starts before the hold time is finished, the object is retriggered.

title: gatemin

messages.description: the gate with a minimum time

ELSE/gatemin.body: [gatemin] allows you to set a minimum gate time value, so if the gate is released before that, it waits for that minimum gate time. If you release after the minimum gate time, then the gate is immediately released. If the gate is reopened before the minimum time, the object is reset and the new gate value takes over.

title: gatemin~

ELSE/gatemin~.body: [gatemin~] allows you to set a minimum gate time value, so if the gate is released before that, it waits for that minimum gate time. If you release after the minimum gate time, then the gate is immediately released. If the gate is reopened before the minimum time, the object is reset and the new gate value takes over.

title: gatenorm
ELSE/gatenorm.body: [gatenorm] normalizes a gate input. By default it normalizes to 1, but you can set other values (0 or negative are ignored). Negative gates are also normalized to a negative value.

title: gatenorm~
ELSE/gatenorm~.body: [gatenorm~] normalizes a gate input. By default it normalizes to 1, but you can set other values (0 or negative are ignored). Negative gates are also normalized to a negative value.

title: gaterelease
ELSE/gaterelease.body: [gaterelease] allows you to release one gate in your patch while you still hold another. [gaterelease] releases a gate value after a given amount of time (specified in ms) after the gate has opened. If the gate is closed before the release time, the object is reset. If the release time is 0 or less, the object is bypassed.

title: gaterelease~
ELSE/gaterelease~.body: [gaterelease~] allows you to release one gate in your patch while you still hold another. [gaterelease~] releases a gate value after a given amount of time (specified in ms) after the gate has opened. If the gate is closed before the release time, the object is reset. If the release time is 0 or less, the object is bypassed.

Its controls set the bandwidth in cents around the input frequency, the number of points in the waveform, the interpolation type and the maximum frequency and amplitude steps.

"Gray Code" is named after Frank Gray, the owner of the patent of gray codes. This type of noise has a high RMS level relative to its peak to peak level. The spectrum is emphasized towards lower frequencies.

ELSE/group~.body: [group~] groups 'n' channels from a multichannel input and sums it. The argument sets the number of output channels. The input is then broken into groups of n channels and summed. For instance "1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6" grouped in a 3 channel output gives us "1+4, 2+5, 3+6" (5, 7, 9). There's a gain compensation factor, set via the 2nd argument or the 'gain' message, which divides by the number of summed channels.

title: hann~
ELSE/hann~.body: [hann~] is an abstraction that applies a Hann window into a signal input. the window size is the same as the block size. This is meant for FFT analysis.

title: hip2~
ELSE/hip2~.body:
[hip2~] is a 1st order highpass filter (1-pole, 1-zero) like [hip~], but with a more accurate frequency response, especially at higher frequencies, and support for multichannel signals.

The filter outputs the same number of channels as the left input. If the right input has more than one channel, the number of channels must match. A single channel gets repeated to match the channels of the left input.

ELSE/meter~.body: [meter~] is a convenient mono VU-meter abstraction based on [vu~] and vanilla's [vu] GUI object. See also [meter2~], [meter4~] and [meter8~].

title: metronome

messages.description: actual beat length, actual tempo and bar duration in ms

methods.description: set time signature symbol and group value

ELSE/metronome.body: [metronome] understands complex time signatures and outputs timeline data (bar, sub-bar, beat and sub-beat count) and phase output. It also syncs to [clock] objects.

title: metronome~
ELSE/metronome~.body: [metronome~] works in conjunction with [metronome] and outputs metronome clicks.

title: midi.clock

messages.description: sets BPM and also sets to internal clock
time interval in BPM from external source

arguments.description: sets BPM and also sets to internal clock

ELSE/midi.clock.body:
[midi.clock] is a MIDI clock abstraction. It works with an internal or external clock (from an external MIDI device). It sends a bang at each MIDI clock and also sends a time interval (in BPM) from external clock sources.
By default, [clock] is set to an external input, which comes from the MIDI device specified in Pd's MIDI configuration. But if you give it a float argument, it sets to internal clock at the BPM specified by the float.

title: midi.in

flags.name: -ext

ELSE/midi.in.body: [midi.in] sends "cooked" MIDI data instead of "raw" data like [midiin] with MIDI data type symbol, values and channel (but a note output is sent as a simple numeric list). It can take a raw MIDI input via its inlet but it also listens to your connected MIDI device.

sent at the end of a sequence

ELSE/midi.body: [midi] plays/records raw MIDI streams and can save/read MIDI files or import/export to txt files.

title: midi.learn

methods.description: print send stored input on right outlet

ELSE/midi.learn.body:
[midi.learn] is an abstraction based on [savestate] that learns and saves any MIDI input data. Activate it via bang or click and send it MIDI data so it learns where it comes from. The information gets stored in the owning patch.
The Learned control/program change are followed by numbers that specify 'control/program number' and 'channel' or just a 'channel number' for note and bend messages (touch and polytouch are not supported).

ELSE/midi.out.body: [midi.out] sends MIDI data from "cooked" data, instead of "raw" data like [midiout]. It takes data type symbol, values and channel (but a note output is received as a simple numeric list). It outputs raw MIDI data but it also sends out to the connected MIDI device.

title: midi2freq
ELSE/midi2freq.body: [midi2freq] converts MIDI to frequency like [mtof], but it also converts lists and allows you so set a different frequency reference value for A4 so you can explore different tunings. Note that 'MIDI cents' are possible, where 69.5 is 50 cents (or a quarter tone) higher than 69 (hence 1 cent = 0.01).

title: midi2note
ELSE/midi2note.description: Convert MIDI pitch to note name
ELSE/midi2note.body: [midi2note] converts a MIDI pitch value to note names (such as Eb3). The names end with an octave number, in a way that middle C (MIDI pitch = 60) represents C4 represents. Float inputs are rounded to integers.

title: mix2~

methods.description: sets gain for channel 1 (range is from 0 to 1)
sets pan for channel 1 (range is from -100 to 100)

ELSE/mix2~.body: [mix2~] is a convenient 2 channel mixer abstraction with gain and panning.

title: mix4~

methods.description: sets gain for channel 1 (range is from 0 to 1)
sets pan for channel 1 (range is from -100 to 100)

ELSE/mix4~.body: [mix4~] is a convenient 4 channel mixer abstraction with gain and panning.

title: mix~
ELSE/mix~.description: mixdown a multichannel input into a stereo output
ELSE/mix~.body: [mix~], for now, takes a MC input and considers them as mono channels that you can set the gain and stereo panning. Later it might take other configurations. The outputs are mono signals for the left and right channels.

title: mono

methods.description: nonzero - legato mode, zero - restores default
sends a note off for the hanging note and clears memory

ELSE/mono.body: [mono] takes note messages and handles them to emulate monophonic synth behavior. Its internal memory can remember up to the last 10 input voices *and pitches need to be >= 0).

title: mono.rev~
ELSE/mono.rev~.body: [mono.rev~] is a reverb abstraction with mono input but stereo output. It's based on a feedback delay network like vanilla's [rev3~] object, but it offers a "room size" parameter whose typical value is around 0.5, values closer to 0 and 1 may create unusual results. Changing size values may generates unusual artifacts (you can clear the delay buffers when you do it to prevent it, but you may get clicks).

title: mono~

methods.description: nonzero sets to legato mode, zero restores default
sends a note off for the hanging note and clears memory

ELSE/mono~.body: [mono~] emulates monophonic synth behaviour and is much like [mono], but can also glide the pitch output with a portamento setting.

title: moog~

methods.description: cutoff frequency in Hz for each channel
clears filter's memory if you blow it up

ELSE/moog~.body: [moog~] is similar and based on [bob~], which emulates moog's resonant lowpass filter. This object is also inspired by VCV's VCF module and has support for multichannels.

title: morph

messages.description: list with one or more elements to morph to

ELSE/morph.body: [morph] is an abstraction based on vanilla's [line], but besides floats, it also works for lists - so you can transition (or morph) between them. It takes a time to reach the target and a grain time just like [line].

title: morph~
ELSE/morph~.body: [morph~] allows you to make a spectral crossfade between the amplitudes and phases of two inputs. You can then do cross synthesis and spectral morphing.

title: mouse
ELSE/mouse.body: [mouse] grabs mouse interaction (click and coordinates). Click and see. This works for any click Pd receives in any window, not only this patch's.

title: mov.avg

messages.description: sets new number of values and clears

ELSE/mov.avg.body: [mov.avg] gives you a running/moving average over the last 'n' values.

title: ms.dec~
ELSE/ms.dec~.body: [ms.dec~] decodes a mid/side signal into a stereo output. It has support for multichannel signals.

title: ms.enc~
ELSE/ms.enc~.body: [ms.enc~] takes a stereo input and encodes into mid and side signals. It has support for multichannel signals.

title: ms2beat

ELSE/ms2beat.body: [ms2beat] converts from ms to beat length according to a BPM value given as an argument or a right inlet.

[ms2samps] is a simple abstraction that converts time values from ms to number of samples.
Conversion expression: samps = ms * samplerate/1000.

messages.description: converted value in number of samples

ELSE/ms2samps~.body:
[ms2samps~] is a simple abstraction that converts time values from ms to number of samples. 
Conversion expression: samps = ms * samplerate/1000.

ELSE/mtx~.body: [mtx~] routes signals from any inlets to one or more outlets. If more than one inlet connects to an outlet, the output is the sum of the inlets' signals. Use [mtx.ctl] to control it.

title: nchs~
ELSE/nchs~.description: get number of channels from multi-channel connections

messages.description: signal to query number of channels

ELSE/nchs~.body: [nchs~] gets the number of channels from a multi-channel connection, as provided by [snake~ in], [clone] or other objects. The object outputs values whenever the DSP chain gets updated and you can also query for the number of channels with a bang message. It also works in subpatches or abstractions because [inlet~] is also multi-channel aware.

title: nlist.append

arguments.description: nested list name to bind to

ELSE/nlist.append.body: [nlist.append] appends elements to a nested list.

title: nlist.define
nlist
ELSE/nlist.define.description: define, store and edit nested lists

methods.description: read a file (no symbol opens dialog window)
save a file (no symbol opens dialog window)
nonzero sets to save contents with the patch

ELSE/nlist.define.body:
[nlist.define] defines a container for multidimensional lists, where brackets set a list as an element. With a given name, the data is shared and can be accessed and changed by the other nlist objects, such as [nlist.get], [nlist.set] and [nlist.len]. Unlike [messcoll], [nlist.define] objects must not share the same name.

By default, the contents are not saved with the patch, but you can change that with the -k flag or the 'keep' message, which remains valid when reopening and resaving the patch. If a file argument is given, the keep flag and message are ignored, since the data is stored in the file.

Clicking on the object opens an editor window. Shift+click opens a dialog window to read a file, and alt+click one to save a file.

title: nlist.delete
ELSE/nlist.delete.description: delete an element of a nested list

arguments.description: nested list name to bind to

ELSE/nlist.delete.body: [nlist.delete] deletes an element from a nested list and takes an index number or list (for nested elements).

title: nlist.depth

arguments.description: nested list name to bind to

ELSE/nlist.depth.body: [nlist.depth] gets the maximum depth level of a nested list. Clicking on the object opens the editor window of the [nlist.define] object with the same name.

title: nlist.flat

messages.description: nested list as a flat list

arguments.description: nested list name to bind to

ELSE/nlist.flat.body: [nlist.flat] outputs the nested list as a flat (one dimensional) list. Clicking on the object opens the editor window of the [nlist.define] object with the same name.

title: nlist.get

arguments.description: nested list name to bind to

ELSE/nlist.get.body:
[nlist.get] gets an element from a nested list. The element can be a list or a nested list, in which case you can give a list index to get a nested element. The '-1' index is a special index that gives you the whole nested list.

The right outlet gives the type of the element (0 for float/symbol, 1 for list, 2 for nested list) or an error (-1 for an out of range index, -2 for an out of depth index). Clicking on the object opens the editor window of the [nlist.define] object with the same name.

title: nlist.insert
ELSE/nlist.insert.description: insert an element in a nested list

arguments.description: nested list name to bind to

ELSE/nlist.insert.body: [nlist.insert] inserts an element in a nested list. The element can be an atom, a list or a nested list. You need to set the index with the 'set' message or argument (default 0) and it can be a float or a list depending on the level.

title: nlist.iter

arguments.description: nested list name to bind to

ELSE/nlist.iter.body: [nlist.iter] iterates through the indexes of a nested list. If an element is nested, the index is a list. You can use [nlist.get] to actually get the element. Clicking on the object opens the editor window of the [nlist.define] object with the same name.

title: nlist.len

messages.description: output nested list's length at top level (same as 0)
index of deeper levels (bang at level 0)

arguments.description: nested list name to bind to

ELSE/nlist.len.body: [nlist.len] gets the length of a nested list. The length counts top level elements, which can be atoms, a list or a nested list on its own. You can query for lengths of deeper levels as well with floats. In this case, a series of floats is output if more than one length is found, and the index list of each is given in the right outlet. Clicking on the object opens the editor window of the [nlist.define] object with the same name.

title: nlist.prepend

arguments.description: nested list name to bind to

ELSE/nlist.prepend.body: [nlist.prepend] prepends elements to a nested list.

title: nlist.set

arguments.description: nested list name to bind to

ELSE/nlist.set.body:
[nlist.set] sets an element of a nested list. The element can be an atom, a list or a nested list. You need to set the index with the 'set' message or argument (default 0) and it can be a float or a list depending on the level. The indexed element must exist.

You can replace a list with a single item, or a nested list with a list or an atom, which removes the further indexes of that list. Conversely, you can put a list or a nested list in the place of an atom and create a list of nested indexes.

title: nlist.traverse

arguments.description: nested list name to bind to

ELSE/nlist.traverse.body: [nlist.traverse] traverses through the indexes of a nested list. A bang goes from top to lower levels (and the level is given on the right outlet), while a float restricts to a given level.

title: nmess

messages.description: resets and sets 'n' number of messages
output a message if the gate is opened
output a message if the gate is closed

ELSE/nmess.body: [nmess] allows 'n' number of messages to be gated through the left outlet (it goes to the right outlet otherwise). A bang in the right inlet resets and reopens the gate.

title: noisegate~

flags.name: -size <float>
flags.description: sets analysis window size in samples (default 512)

ELSE/noisegate~.body: [noisegate~] is a noise gate abstraction. It takes a threshold in dBFS in which it only audio through that has a RMS value over that threshold.

title: nop~
ELSE/nop~.body: [nop~] does no operation, that is, it does nothing. It's mostly useful for managing singal cords in your patch.

title: norm~

flags.name: -size <float>
flags.description: sets analysis window size in ms (default 10)

ELSE/norm~.body: [norm~] is a normalizer abstraction based on [mov.rms~]. It takes a normalization value in dBFS and a window analysis size.

ELSE/note.in.body: [note.in] extracts MIDI Pitch information from external "raw" MIDI data or an internally connected device. It deals with both NoteOn and NoteOff messages (with release velocity).

title: note2midi
ELSE/note2midi.description: convert note name to MIDI pitch

messages.description: note name to convert to MIDI pitch

ELSE/note2midi.body: [note2midi] converts note names (such as 'C4') to MIDI pitch values. All enharmonic names are included (even unusual ones like Cb and double sharps/flats). It takes symbols, lists or anythings that end with an octave number, in a way that C4 represents middle C (MIDI pitch = 60). Range is from C0 to B8.

title: notedur2ratio
ELSE/notedur2ratio.description: convert note duration to fraction or float

messages.description: in note duration syntax to convert
converted duration to fraction or float

ELSE/notedur2ratio.body: [notedur2ratio] converts from a note duration syntax to a fractional notation or a float. The syntax is: '1n' for whole note, '2n' for half note, '4n' for quarter note, '8n' for eighth note (and so on down to 128n). Dotted notes are possible and you can add tuplets to the symbol in the [x:y] format or you can add the following letters to specify most common tuplets: 'd' for duplet, 't' for triplet, 'q' for quintuplet, 's' for septuplet and 'n' for nonuplet. Tied notes are also possible with "_".

title: osc.format
ELSE/osc.format.body: [osc.format] is similar to Vanilla's [oscformat]. This is still way too simple and experimental. It is used in the [osc.send] abstraction and can be used for edge and lower level cases. It takes anything messages or lists whose first element is an address that start with "/". The type of data for each element in the message is either a float or a string only depending on the atom type, so there are only these options (so far). You can't send bundles either. Use the original Vanilla [oscformat] or mrpeach's packOSC object for more complete objects.

title: osc.parse
ELSE/osc.parse.body: [osc.parse] is similar to Vanilla's [oscparse] but the output is not a list and more closely related on how OSC messages are generally dealt with. It is still in the [osc.receive] abstraction and you can use the object for more edge and lower level cases.

title: osc.receive

arguments.description: port to connect to at load time

ELSE/osc.receive.body: [osc.receive] receives OSC messages from network connections and is an abstraction based on [osc.parse] and [netreceive].

title: osc.route

ELSE/osc.route.body: [osc.route] routes OSC messages received from [osc.receive]. It follows the same logic as Vanilla's [route] where arguments set the number of outlets and an extra is created for no matches. The difference is that it manages OSC addresses instead, specified with the "/" separator. Note how the '/hz' address matches input messages that start with '/hz' even if it has further sub addresses.

title: osc.send

arguments.description: address/port to connect to at load time

ELSE/osc.send.body: [osc.send] sends OSC messages over the network and is an abstraction based on [osc.format] and [netsend].

ELSE/pack2.body: [pack2] is kinda similar to Pd Vanilla's [pack], but any inlet triggers the output (though a "set" message avoids the output). It can also initialize a symbol value and it doesn't create a list selector for you. Moreover, you can change many elements with a list message and an element that was initialized as a float can become a symbol and vice versa.

title: packet~
ELSE/packet~.body: [packet~] is a formant oscillator where you specify the fundamental (f0) frequency, the center (or formant) frequency as a ratio and the bandwidth. The object has support for multichannels.

title: pad

messages.description: report mouse button press <1> and release <0>

ELSE/pad.body: [pad] is a GUI object that reports mouse coordinates over its area and click status. If you click and drag, you can get values outside the GUI area.

title: paf~

arguments.description: phase shift from fundamental for formant frequency

methods.description: reset phase for fundamental and optionally shift for formant frequency

ELSE/paf~.body: [paf~] is a formant oscillator where you specify the fundamental (f0) frequency, the center (or formant) frequency and the bandwidth (around the center frequency). All these parameters are in Hz. This technique is used to synthesize vocal sounds. The object has support for multichannels.

title: pan.mc~
ELSE/pan.mc~.description: circular panning over given number of channels
ELSE/pan.mc~.body: [pan.mc~] pans an input signal to 'n' channels of a multichannel output, with equal power crossfading between adjacent channels according to a spread parameter. The speakers are assumed to be in a circle with equal angles between them, so the position input goes around the circle: it ranges from 0 to 1, where 1 is the same as 0.

title: pan.stereo~
ELSE/pan.stereo~.body: [pan.stereo~] sets the stereo input pan which merges both channels to the left or right. It uses sin/cos equal power panning.

title: panic

messages.description: sends note off for hanging notes

methods.description: clears the hanging notes that [midiflush] keeps track of

ELSE/panic.body: Like a "panic button", [panic] keeps track of raw Note-on messages that weren't switched off and "flushes" them by sending corresponding note-offs when it receives a bang.

title: pan~
ELSE/pan~.description: circular panning over given number of channels
ELSE/pan~.body: [pan~] pans an input signal to 'n' outlets, with equal power crossfading between adjacent channels according to a spread parameter. The speakers are assumed to be in a circle with equal angles between them, so the position input goes around the circle: it ranges from 0 to 1, where 1 is the same as 0.

title: parabolic~

flags.name: -midi
flags.description: sets frequency input in MIDI pitch

flags.name: -mc <list>
flags.description: sets multichannel output with a list of frequencies

methods.description: nonzero sets frequency input in MIDI pitch
<channel, freq> set a single frequency channel
nonzero sets to soft sync mode

ELSE/parabolic~.body: [parabolic~] is a parabolic oscillator that accepts negative frequencies, has inlets for phase sync and phase modulation. A parabolic waveform is similar to a sinusoid but it is not band limited (has aliasing).

title: pattern

messages.description: nonzero starts, zero stops the sequencer
bang or index float at every new note

ELSE/pattern.body: [pattern] is a rhythmic pattern sequencer. The note durations are specified as floats or fractions (where '1' is a whole note), negative values are rests! A '|' separates into different bars. When you set a new pattern via the right inlet, it only starts when the previous one ends.

title: pdlink
ELSE/pdlink.description: send messages across network by name
ELSE/pdlink.body: [pdlink] allows you to communicate to/from different Pd instances over local network, as different versions and even forks of Pure Data (such as plugdata). It works like [send]/[receive] (or [else/sender]/[else/receiver]) as it just needs a symbol address. It works via network but it's simpler as it doesn't require network or OSC configuration! It also allows you to communicate to a [pd~] subprocess.

title: pdlink~
ELSE/pdlink~.description: send messages across network by name

flags.name: -compress
flags.description: apply Opus compression to audio stream

ELSE/pdlink~.body: [pdlink~] allows you to send/receive audio streams to/from different Pd instances, as different versions, platforms and even forks of Pure Data (such as plugdata). It works like [send~]/[receive~] as it just needs a symbol address. It works via network but it's simpler as it doesn't require network configuration! It also allows you to communicate to a [pd~] subprocess. You can make up to 16 sends to a single receive, but you can receive as many times as you like.

title: peak~

flags.name: -lin
flags.description: sets the output to linear (default dBFS)

methods.description: sets window and hop size in samples

ELSE/peak~.body: [peak~] is similar to Pd Vanilla's [env~], but it reports the peak amplitude value in linear (default) or dBFS.

title: perlin~

methods.description: a float sets seed, no float sets a unique internal

ELSE/perlin~.body: [perlin~] is an abstraction that implements 1-dimensional Perlin Noise (a type of gradient noise developed by Ken Perlin). It uses [white~] as a noise source into a sample and hold function and generates smoothened functions according to a frequency value in Hz (values under 0 and above Nyquist are aliased).

title: pgm.in

flags.name: -ext
flags.description: only listen to external input source (default no)

methods.description: nonzero sets to listen only to external input source

ELSE/pgm.in.body: [pgm.in] extracts MIDI Program information from raw MIDI input (such as from [midiin]). Unlike vanilla's [pgmin] and [pgmout], the program change values are from 0 to 127!

title: pgm.out

methods.description: nonzero sets to listen only to external mode

ELSE/pgm.out.body: [pgm.out] formats and sends raw MIDI program messages. An argument sets channel number (the default is 1). Unlike vanilla's [pgmin] and [pgmout], the program change values are from 0 to 127!

title: phaser.m~
ELSE/phaser.m~.body: [phaser.m~] is a MERDA module wrapper around [phaser~], a phaser effect.

title: phaser~

methods.description: number of stages (needs to be a multiple of 2)

ELSE/phaser~.body: [phaser~] is a mono phaser effect abstraction. You can set the number of stages with the first argument, which sets the order of the internal allpass filter (needs to be a multiple of 2). It requires a signal LFO to control the frequency sweep.

title: phaseseq~
ELSE/phaseseq~.body: [phaseseq~] takes a list of thresholds and outputs impulses when reaching the threshold values.

title: phasor
ELSE/phasor.body: This is like the [phasor~] but operates in a control rate (with a maximum resolution of 1 ms).

title: pi

messages.description: calculate or output the last calculated value

ELSE/pi.body: [pi] calculates and outputs the value of pi. It receives a multiplier value via the argument or second inlet, which needs to be greater than 0 (otherwise it's considered as 1).

title: pic

messages.description: open an image file named by the symbol
a bang is output if you click on the image
pic width/height when in report size mode

flags.name: -open <symbol>
flags.description: sets file name to open (default empty)

flags.name: -outline
flags.description: sets to outline mode (default no outline)

flags.name: -size
flags.description: sets to "report size" mode (default no report)

methods.description: open an image file named by the symbol
nonzero sets to report size mode

ELSE/pic.body: [pic] loads image pictures that you can interact with. It only works with file types: .gif, .ppm & .pgm. you click on the picture and it sends a bang (default) or 1 when clicking and 0 when releasing (when in latch mode).

title: pick

messages.description: the element from the input message

ELSE/pick.body: [pick] picks an element from an input message according to an element number. Negative values count from last to the first element. If you ask for an element number out of the range, nothing is output.

title: pick~
ELSE/pick~.description: pick a channel from a multichannel connection
ELSE/pick~.body: [pick~] picks a channel from a multichannel connection. The channel is specified via argument or float input and is indexed from 1 (0 gives "none"). Negative values count from last to the first element. If you ask for an element number out of the range, you also get "none".

title: pimp

messages.description: output a bang at period transitions

ELSE/pimp.body: This is like the [pimp~] but operates in a control rate (with a maximum resolution of 1 ms).

title: pimpmul~
ELSE/pimpmul~.body: [pimpmul~] is a "pimp~" multiplier. The [pimp~] object from ELSE is both a [phasor~] and an [imp~] oscillator. Use [pimpul~] to keep [phasor~] or [pimp~] objects in sync with different frequency ratios.

title: pimp~

flags.name: -mc <list>
flags.description: sets multichannel output with a list of frequencies

flags.name: -midi
flags.description: sets frequency input in MIDI pitch (default Hz)

flags.name: -soft
flags.description: sets to soft sync mode (default hard)

methods.description: nonzero sets to frequency input in MIDI pitch
<channel, freq> set a single frequency channel
nonzero sets to soft sync mode

ELSE/pimp~.body: [pimp~] is a combination of [phasor~] and [imp~] (alias of [impulse~]). It's [imp~] with an extra phase output (left outlet). The impulse happens at every phase period start (in both negative or positive frequencies/directions). It also has inlets for phase sync and phase modulation like [imp~].

title: ping.pong~
ELSE/ping.pong~.body: [ping.pong~] is a ping pong delay object

title: pink~

methods.description: a float sets seed, no float sets a unique internal

ELSE/pink~.body: [pink~] is a pink noise generator, which sounds less hissy than white noise (but not as less as brown~). White noise has constant spectral power, but pink noise has constant power per octave and it decrease 3dB per octave. Like other noise objects, this is based on a pseudo random number generator algorithm.

title: pipe2
ELSE/pipe2.body: [pipe2] is similar to vanilla's pipe. It takes all kinds of messages and delays them.

title: pitch.shift~
ELSE/pitch.shift~.body: [pitch.shift~] is a pitch shifter abstraction based on granulation. You can set a transposition factor in cents and a grain size in ms.

title: plaits.m~
ELSE/plaits.m~.body: [plaits.m~] is a MERDA module wrapper around [plaits~], a macro oscillator with many synthesis models, made polyphonic and easier to use. It can be played via MIDI or with signals for pitch, trigger and level. The other inlets modulate FM, timbre, harmonics and morph through attenuverters; connecting to them activates the modulation automatically.

title: plaits~

messages.description: note on/off messages with pitch and velocity
level for built-in VCA or excitation signal
output info on setting model or 'dump'

flags.description: sets pitch input to CV (default Hz)

flags.name: -midi
flags.description: sets pitch input to MIDI (default Hz)

ELSE/plaits~.body: [plaits~] is based on the "Plaits" module from Mutable Instruments.

title: plate.rev.m~
ELSE/plate.rev.m~.body: [plate.rev.m~] is a MERDA module wrapper around [plate.rev~], a plate reverb with mono input and stereo output. It has no CV inputs yet, so it works like an effect pedal.

title: plate.rev~
ELSE/plate.rev~.body: [plate.rev~] is a reverb abstraction based on a patch by Tom Erbe implementing the plate reverb model by Dattorro. It has a mono input and stereo output.

title: play.file~

messages.description: a bang when finishing playing the sample

arguments.default: 1 if no file is given, or sound file's if given

arguments.description: the name of the file to open

methods.description: resume playback where it was paused
opens a file with the symbol name (no symbol opens dialog box)
sets a file to open next time it starts playing

ELSE/play.file~.body: [play.file~] is a convenient abstraction based on [readsf~] to read files from your computer. Note that the file sample needs to be at the same sample rate as Pd's. The object can open files with absolute paths and is also able to search for files relative to the parent patch.

title: player~

messages.description: a bang when finishing playing the buffer

arguments.default: 1 if no file is given, or sound file's if given

arguments.description: the name of the file to open

if no float is given, plays whole file. 1st float sets start, 2nd sets end (in ms) and 3rd sets speed rate
stops playing and outputs 0 (cannot be resumed)
pauses at a particular point (can be resumed)

ELSE/player~.body: [player~] is a convenient abstraction based on [soundfiler] and [tabplayer~]. It's much more versatile than [play.file~]. For instance, you can play in different speeds and backwards.

title: pluck.m~
ELSE/pluck.m~.body: [pluck.m~] is a MERDA module wrapper around [pluck~], a plucked string. It can be played via MIDI, with a number of voices (1 by default), or with signals for pitch and trigger. CV inputs set the decay time in ms and the filter cutoff in Hz, and the right inlet takes a signal to excite the string.

title: pluck~

messages.description: set frequency and trigger value (normalized to MIDI range)

flags.name: -in

nonzero forces MIDI input over signal

ELSE/pluck~.body: [pluck~] is a Karplus-Strong algorithm with a 1st order lowpass filter in the feedback loop. It takes frequency in Hz or MIDI, a decay time in ms and a cutoff frequency in Hz for the filter. It is triggered by signals at zero to nonzero transitions or by lists at control rate.

title: pm2~

set op volume ('pan1' sets op1, etc)

ELSE/pm2~.body: [pm2~] is a 2 operators FM (actually phase modulation) synthesizer. Each oscillator can modulate itself and each other.

title: pm4~

set op detuning ('detune1' sets op1, etc)
set op panning ('pan1' sets op1, etc)
set op volume ('pan1' sets op1, etc)

ELSE/pm4~.body: [pm4~] is a 4 operator FM (actually phase modulation) synthesizer. Each oscillator can modulate itself and the others.

title: pm6.m~
ELSE/pm6.m~.body: [pm6.m~] is a six-operator FM (actually phase modulation) synthesizer module in the style of the DX7, with stereo output. A matrix sets the modulation index between the operators, including self feedback, and each operator has its own ratio, level and panning. The left inlet takes pitch in MIDI, and the other inlets set the level of each operator and the master level, which is 1 when nothing is connected.

title: pm6~

methods.description: set index ('1to2' sets op1 to op2 index, etc)
set op ratio ('ratio1' sets op1, etc)
set op detuning ('detune1' sets op1, etc)

set op volume ('pan1' sets op1, etc)

ELSE/pm6~.body: [pm6~] is a 4 operators FM (actually phase modulation) synthesizer. Each oscillator can modulate itself and each other.

title: pm~

messages.description: modulation frequency as a ratio of the carrier frequency

arguments.description: modulation frequency as a ratio of the carrier frequency

ELSE/pm~.body: [pm~] is a very basic and simple phase modulation unit, which consists of a pair of sinusoidal oscillators, where one modulates the phase input of another.

title: pol2car

phase (in radians) from the polar coordinates

imaginary part of the Cartesian form

ELSE/pol2car.body: [pol2car] converts polar coordinates (amplitude / phase) to Cartesian coordinates (real / imaginary).

title: pol2car~

messages.description: amplitude of the signal in the polar form
phase (in radians) of the signal in the polar form
real part of the signal in the Cartesian form
imaginary part of the signal in the Cartesian form

ELSE/pol2car~.body: [pol2car~] converts polar coordinates (amplitude / phase) to Cartesian coordinates (real / imaginary).

title: polymetro

messages.description: syncs (restarts count) when polymetro is on
multiplier as a float or fraction (anything/symbol)

flags.name: -b
flags.description: sets to bang mode output (instead of floats)

ELSE/polymetro.body: [polymetro] is a polyrhythmic metronome. Polyrhythms are better specified with fractions, but you can set it as floats, which is a tempo multiplier value in the end. The left output is a counter for the base tempo count while the right outlet is the relative count/tempo as specified by the multiplier ratio. This is an abstraction based on synced [clock] objects.

title: polymetro~

messages.description: multiplier as a float or fraction (anything/symbol/float)

ELSE/polymetro~.body: [polymetro~] is a polyrhythmic metronome for signal rate that outputs impulses. Polyrhythms are better specified with fractions, but you can set it as floats, which is a tempo multiplier value in the end. The left output is a counter for the base tempo count while the right outlet is the relative count/tempo as specified by the ratio. This is an abstraction based on [pimp~] and [pimpmul~] objects.

You can choose by clicking on the selected item or via up/down arrow keys and hitting 'enter'. By default, the output is the index, but can also be the element or both.

title: power~

messages.description: the signal raised to the given power

ELSE/power~.body: [power~] is a power function waveshaper for signals that extends the usual definition of exponentiation and returns -pow(-a, b) when you have a negative signal input. This allows not only the output of negative values but also the exponentiation of negative values by non-integer exponents.

ELSE/presets.body: [presets] manages presets for patches and abstractions and has interpolation and morphing features.

title: presets.m
ELSE/presets.m.body: [presets.m] manages presets for MERDA modules: put it last in your patch, save and reopen it, then choose a preset number and click to save a preset. The parameters of all MERDA modules in the patch are saved with it and restored when you open it again.

title: properties

messages.description: bang when asked for properties in the parent patch

ELSE/properties.body: [properties] sends a bang when you put it in an abstraction or a subpatch and ask for properties on the parent patch (by selecting the "properties" option after right clicking). This is useful for making properties for graphical subpatches or abstractions.

title: ptouch.in

ELSE/ptouch.in.body: [ptouch.in] extracts MIDI polyphonic aftertouch information from raw MIDI input (such as from [midiin]).

title: ptouch.out

methods.description: nonzero sets to listen only to external mode

ELSE/ptouch.out.body: [ptouch.out] formats and sends raw MIDI polyphonic aftertouch messages. An argument sets channel number (the default is 1).

title: pulse
ELSE/pulse.body: This is much like the [pulse~] oscillator but operates in a control rate (with a default resolution of 1 ms) and the output is like a toggle switch.

title: pulsecount~

ELSE/pulsecount~.body: [pulsecount~] counts pulse triggers. A trigger happens at transitions from non positive to positive. A trigger in the right inlet resets the counter to zero. The argument sets a maximum count value (if greater than 0).

title: pulsediv~

messages.description: an impulse resets the counter to the start value
impulse for the other trigger inputs

ELSE/pulsediv~.body: [pulsediv~] outputs impulses when receiving triggers (signal changes from non-positive to positive). The left outlet outputs impulses according to the division value and the right outlet outputs impulses for the other trigger inputs.

nonzero sets to soft sync mode

title: pvoc.freeze~
ELSE/pvoc.freeze~.body: [pvoc.freeze~] is a freeze object based on a phase vocoder.

title: pvoc.live~

messages.description: resets to the beginning of the delay line

ELSE/pvoc.live~.body: [pvoc.live~] is like [pvoc.player~], but for live input. It provides independent time stretching and pitch shifting via granulation.

title: pvretune~

ELSE/pvretune~.body: [pvretune~] retunes partials of an input sound and resynthesises via a phase vocoder oscillator bank. The default is the 12-tone equal temperament but you can set any arbitrary scale with a list of frequencies. This is based on Eric Lyon's [fftease/pvtuner~]. There's support for multichanels.

title: quantizer
ELSE/quantizer.body: [quantizer] approximates a value to step values defined by the argument. There are 4 approximation modes: round (default), int, floor, ceil or both.

title: quantizer~
ELSE/quantizer~.body: [quantizer~] approximates a value to step values defined by the argument. There are 4 approximation modes: round (default), int, floor, ceil or both.

title: rad2deg
ELSE/rad2deg.body: [rad2deg] converts radians (0 to 2*pi) to radians (0 to 360). Besides 0 to 2*pi you can also convert negative values from 0 to -2*pi (0 to -360) - and input values are wrapped if the exceed this input range. If you give it the '-pos' flag, which wraps to positive values only.

title: rad2hz
ELSE/rad2hz.body:
Use [rad2hz] to convert a signal representing a frequency in "Radians per Sample" to Hz. This depends on the patch's sample rate (sr). The conversion formula is;
hz = rad * sr / 2pi

title: rampnoise

ELSE/rampnoise.body: [rampnoise] is a control rate ramp noise. It doesn't need the DSP on to function. Give it a seed value if you want a reproducible output.

ELSE/rampnoise~.body:
[rampnoise~] is a low frequency (band limited) noise generator with interpolation, therefore it ramps from one random value to another, resulting in random ramps. Random values are between -1 and 1 at a rate in Hz (negative frequencies accepted). Use the seed message if you want a reproducible output.
The [rampnoise~] object produces frequencies limited to a band from 0 up to the frequency it is running. It can go up to the sample rate, and when that happens, it's basically a white noise generator.
